mutant.description: Each instrument this wave lands carries an arm that FIRES and a control that shows the arm could have failed. arm_census.py --self-test drives four clauses: SPLIT (an escaped pipe must not add a cell; control -- a naive split DOES add one), MULT (x N expands to N; control -- a bare token expands to 1), DEDUP (a token cited twice counts once; control -- two distinct tokens count two), SLICE (a non-arm pipe-row is REFUSED not silently discarded; control -- a numbered row is still accepted). build_manifest.py --check carries its own negative arm (--plant-missing). run_battery.py distinguishes NOT_EXERCISABLE from both pass and fail rather than collapsing them. INSTRUMENT LIMITS, stated so these are not credited with reach they lack: arm_census.py measures sec 3's ARM TABLE only. Its dedup clause had never been exercised by any corpus (0 double-cited at six consecutive pins) until this wave drove it synthetically -- six clean readings do not test a branch none of them enter. carrier_dependency.py is a LOWER BOUND, not a measurement: it reads what a row NAMES, and a row can exercise a type without naming it (row 4). Its output is not used as AC3's value. The escaped-pipe split is now live-relevant: sec 3b landed the FIRST escaped pipe inside the 3..4 span at 55a20db49e (R4-DT-4). This census is unaffected because the slice now cuts at any heading level AND the row filter is numeric-only -- two independent reasons, one of which I discovered I had been relying on without designing it.
mutant.expected: 4 of 4 census clauses OK with every control reachable; manifest VALID positive and INVALID negative; runner exit 3 rather than 0 or 1.
mutant.observed: 4 of 4 OK (rc 0). Manifest VALID (rc 0) / INVALID on a planted miss (rc 1). Runner exit 3 with 'verdict WITHHELD'. THE SLICE CONTROL EARNED ITS PLACE IMMEDIATELY: it FIRED on my own first fix, which cut at the next '## ' heading and missed that sec 3b is a THREE-hash '### 3b.' -- 14 foreign rows still reached the parser. Without the control I would have shipped a 'tightened' boundary still swallowing the addendum, with the numbers looking correct because the numeric row filter was quietly saving me.

surprises: R4-DT-3 (BLOCKING, issuer-ruled): AC3 is not dischargeable by any text instrument. My classifier gave a FALSE PLUS38_ONLY on row 4, and the schema-derived vocabulary collides on opened/closed across two carriers. I reported by confidence tier rather than filing a column I could not defend, and said plainly that I did not believe the mechanical 11/2 result.

R4-DT-4 (OBSERVATION): sec 3b landed the span's FIRST escaped pipe. My census was immune -- but by the row filter's numeric shape, i.e. a naming convention in someone else's addendum, not by anything this file guaranteed. Reported to every seat that slices sec 3, and the dependency is now enforced by a control rather than relied upon.

R4-DT-5 (ACCEPTED): the TO's own AC8 command cannot measure AC8. A git pathspec * crosses directory separators, and the extension globs miss run_gates.sh -- a bundle member. Discharged on the member-list intersection instead.

MY OWN CONDUCT, twice in ten minutes: I printed 'empty = no member changed' beneath output showing 8 files, then 'EMPTY = ...' beneath output showing 14. Both labels were composed before their evidence and neither was reread against it. Nothing propagated -- I caught both on reading and the final measurement is sound -- but it is CLAUDE.md's never-compose-a-report-in-the-same-call-as-the-act, broken by me, in the wave whose whole subject is derived-not-typed numbers.

My proposed remedy for R4-DT-3 (have the design's author state it per row) was DECLINED by the issuer as the typed-beside-derived class -- correctly, and on the rule I have been filing against all round. It was then taken in a form that answers the objection: an ARTIFACT with a stated falsifier (sec 3b), carried as INFERRED with promote-or-kill, which is not the same thing as prose beside a measurement.
